options.headline: LESS FEAR, MORE EVIDENCE
options.text: Most AI headlines are about risk, jobs and runaway machines. The story below is quieter and more useful. At two UK hospitals, an AI tool helped sort urgent skin cancer referrals, clearing benign cases and freeing specialist time for more than 8,500 extra appointments. It is one measured result, with its limits stated plainly. That kind of evidence deserves more attention than the next prediction.

options.headline: TIME GIVEN BACK TO CARE
options.text: The best use of AI is not replacing the people who care for us. It is giving them back the time to do it. At two UK hospitals, an AI tool cleared benign skin referrals so dermatologists could offer more than 8,500 extra appointments to the patients who need them most. The purpose stays human. The technology clears the path.

options.headline: WHERE WOULD THE TIME GO?
options.text: If a tool could take routine checks off a specialist's desk, where would you want that time to go? At two UK hospitals, an AI tool cleared benign skin referrals and freed enough dermatologist time for more than 8,500 extra appointments over 16 months. The result below is real and measured. The harder question is what we choose to do with the time it gives back.

options.headline: THE QUIET WORK OF TRIAGE
options.text: The most useful AI in medicine is often the least dramatic. It does not take the spotlight or the final call. It sorts, so that people with real problems reach a specialist sooner. The story below shows that in practice: at two UK hospitals, AI triage of skin referrals freed time for more than 8,500 extra appointments, with its misses reported openly.

options.headline: AI THAT MAKES ROOM
options.text: At two UK hospitals, AI cleared benign skin referrals and made room for more than 8,500 extra specialist appointments.

stories.headline: AI clears benign skin referrals, freeing time for 8,500 more UK appointments
stories.why: Real-world study of 8,391 patients at 2 UK hospitals over 16 months, EADV Congress 2026
stories.bullet: 8,500 more skin appointments, as AI cleared benign referrals at 2 UK hospitals
texts:
An autonomous AI triaged 8,391 urgent skin cancer referrals at two UK hospitals over 16 months. It discharged 25 to 31% of patients with benign lesions without clinician review, saving an estimated 2,851 hours of specialist time: enough for more than 8,500 extra face-to-face appointments.

Sensitivity for invasive melanoma, SCC and BCC was above 98%.

#AIforGood

Waiting to hear whether a mole is cancer is hard. At two UK hospitals, an AI reviews images of referred skin lesions and can discharge people with benign ones without waiting for a specialist.

Over 16 months that freed enough dermatologist time for more than 8,500 extra appointments, so specialists can focus on the patients who need them most.

#AIforGood

What if the wait for a skin cancer check could get shorter for everyone? In a real-world study at two UK hospitals, an autonomous AI discharged a quarter to a third of urgent referrals with benign lesions, freeing 2,851 hours of specialist time across 8,391 patients.

Six missed cases were later picked up through monitoring, with no harm reported.

#AIforGood
